Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old male lawyer with several months of low mood, low appetite/weight loss, reduced energy and intermittent palpitations/shortness of breath (episodic, notable in lifts); patient has known hypothyroidism but stopped thyroxine and has had no recent blood tests — clinician arranged general bloods and advised follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: progressive low mood, low appetite, low energy/fatigue for months; intermittent palpitations and sensation of breathlessness; intermittent nausea; unintentional weight loss.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Low mood and low energy: "long, long ago," worsened around job change; patient estimates ~3–6 months of notable symptoms.
  - Appetite change began ~3.5 months ago after changing to a new law firm.
  - Weight loss approximately 1 stone over ~6 months.
  - Palpitations/shortness of breath: episodic, occurs notably in lifts/closed spaces and when he feels unwell; not exertional — patient can walk about 1 mile without shortness of breath.
  - Stopped taking thyroxine since changing GP (timeframe coincides with recent changes; no recent thyroid blood tests).
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Palpitations triggered by being in lifts/when feeling unwell.
  - No clear relieving factors documented.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - Nausea intermittently, occasional headaches.
  - Some reduction in sexual/nightly activity reported by wife.
- Pertinent negatives (documented):
  - No chest pain.
  - No cough.
  - No vomiting.
  - Bowel habits described as normal; no diarrhoea, no blood or mucus in stool.
  - No recent blood tests performed.
  - No allergies documented in transcript.
  - No smoking/alcohol/substance use documented.
  - No suicidal ideation or self-harm discussed/documented.

Past Medical History:
- Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid) — previously treated with thyroxine.
  - Patient reports he stopped taking thyroxine since changing doctors; no recent thyroid function tests.
- No other chronic medical conditions documented.

Medications:
- Thyroxine — dose/route/frequency not documented; patient reports he is currently NOT taking it.
- No other current or recent medications recorded.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Social History:
- Age 35, male, married.
- Occupation: lawyer; recent job change (new law firm) preceded symptom onset/worsening.
- Decreased physical activity recently; reports not been walking lately.
- Wife has noticed decreased nightly sexual activity.
- Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use: not recorded.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- No investigations/results recorded at time of consult.
- Planned/ordered by clinician: general bloods including FBC, renal function, liver function, thyroid function tests (TFTs), vitamin levels (clinician phrasing: “general set of bloods” including anaemia, kidney, liver, vitamin levels).  
- Plan to consider physical examination after blood results if bloods are unremarkable.
- Administrative: patient instructed to call support via app to arrange blood tests; clinician to submit form; patient will receive text to book follow-up appointment after results.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
- Working impression: depressive syndrome (possible major depressive disorder) in the context of untreated/unstable thyroid disease (patient stopped thyroxine) with episodic palpitations/shortness of breath that may represent situational anxiety/panic or cardiac arrhythmia — initial approach focused on blood tests to exclude medical contributors.

DDx Integration (brief):
- Major depressive disorder (High likelihood)
  - Supporting: persistent low mood, reduced appetite, weight loss (~1 stone), low energy for months, functional impact (relationship/nightly activity affected), onset/worsening after job change.
  - Opposing: no explicit documentation of anhedonia, sleep disturbance or suicidality (not asked/documented).
- Thyroid dysfunction due to stopping thyroxine (Medium–High likelihood)
  - Supporting: known hypothyroidism, patient stopped thyroxine, no recent TFTs; symptoms of low energy and low mood compatible.
  - Opposing: some symptoms (weight loss, palpitations) are atypical for hypothyroidism and could suggest alternate thyroid states or other causes — DDx notes this inconsistency (conflict noted).
- Anxiety disorder / situational panic (Medium likelihood)
  - Supporting: episodic palpitations and breathlessness particularly in lifts (closed spaces) and when unwell.
  - Opposing: lack of classic panic cognitions recorded; palpitations could be medical in origin.

Issue 1: Low mood / possible depressive disorder
- Assessment:
  - Clinical picture consistent with depressive syndrome of several months’ duration with functional impact.
  - Medical contributors (thyroid dysfunction, anaemia, vitamin deficiency) need exclusion.
- Plan:
  - Arrange general blood tests (FBC, U&E, LFTs, TFTs, vitamin levels) via support as clinician initiated; patient to call support number in app to book.
  - Review blood results and arrange follow-up appointment (patient will receive text to book once results are available).
  - If bloods are normal, clinician plans in-person physical examination and further mental health assessment.
  - Safety net: advise patient to seek urgent care (A&E) for chest pain or severe cardiorespiratory symptoms; contact the practice if symptoms worsen, bowel changes occur, or vomiting develops.
  - Documentation gap: formal risk assessment for self-harm/suicidality not documented; consider addressing at follow-up.

Issue 2: Stopped thyroxine / possible thyroid dysfunction
- Assessment:
  - Patient has known hypothyroidism and reports stopping thyroxine since changing GP; no recent TFTs.
  - Thyroid abnormalities could account for fatigue/mood changes; some symptoms (weight loss, palpitations) are less typical for hypothyroidism and raise possibility of alternate thyroid states or mixed causes (DDx flagged this).
- Plan:
  - Include thyroid function tests (TFTs) in ordered bloods.
  - Do not restart/alter thyroxine without review of TFTs and primary care/GP input (no medication changes documented in consult).
  - Review TFTs promptly and coordinate with patient’s GP for medication reconciliation and management.

Issue 3: Episodic palpitations and shortness of breath (not exertional)
- Assessment:
  - Episodes described as rapid heartbeat and feeling unable to breathe, often in lifts/closed spaces and when feeling unwell; no chest pain or syncope; preserved exercise tolerance (can walk ~1 mile).
  - Differential includes situational anxiety/panic and intermittent arrhythmia; medical causes (thyroid dysfunction, anaemia, other) need exclusion.
- Plan:
  - Initial investigation via blood tests (TFTs, FBC, electrolytes) to exclude metabolic/endocrine causes.
  - Safety net: advise A&E attendance for chest pain, syncope, severe breathlessness, or if palpitations become persistent/significantly worse.
  - If palpitations persist or increase after initial tests/assessment, consider ECG and further cardiac evaluation (arrhythmia workup) — to be arranged based on results and follow-up assessment.

General plan items:
- Patient instructed to call support via the app to arrange blood tests; clinician will submit required forms.
- Patient to receive a text message after results are available to book follow-up appointment.
- If blood tests are normal, arrange in-person physical examination and further investigations as indicated.
- Safety netting reiterated: A&E for chest pain or acute severe symptoms; contact practice for changes in bowel habits, vomiting, or clinical deterioration.

Quality checks:
- Missing but expected elements: vitals and physical examination findings, detailed medication dose/route/frequency, allergies clarification, smoking/alcohol/substance history, formal suicidality/self-harm risk assessment — not documented in transcript.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: DDx notes that weight loss and palpitations are atypical for hypothyroidism and may suggest alternate thyroid status or other causes — potential inconsistency with patient’s report of stopped thyroxine and hypothyroid history (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: audio generally understandable though some brief inaudible exchanges; no recorded objective measurements or tests.
